thinkingMessage.text: Checking bench entrypoints and build scripts to locate Go tooling.

success.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# bench-cursor entrypoint: bridge on in-container loopback (its own security
# stance — 0.0.0.0 refused without an unexposed option) + a socat relay on
# 0.0.0.0:7790 that docker publishes to HOST loopback only. The ready line
# rides container stderr (docker logs) for the driver to parse.
set -euo pipefail
/bridge/bin/cursor-sdk-bridge --workspace /bench/repo --state-root /tmp/cursor-state --verbose &
BRIDGE_PID=$!
# wait for the listener before opening the relay
for i in $(seq 1 50); do
  if socat -u OPEN:/dev/null TCP:127.0.0.1:7788,connect-timeout=1 2>/dev/null; then break; fi
  sleep 0.2
done
exec socat TCP-LISTEN:7790,fork,reuseaddr,bind=0.0.0.0 TCP:127.0.0.1:7788

thinkingMessage.text:
A Perl script will perform Go static call analysis.

The script will scan all .go files while excluding vendor directories. Each file will be parsed to extract package names, import paths, aliases, and declarations including functions and methods. Calls will be resolved to their full target identifiers. This approach rigorously distinguishes declarations from calls.

The script will recognize Go call patterns including same-package, qualified, and method invocations. It will track the current function context to identify callers, treating nested function literals as callers of their enclosing functions. Test files will be included as callers.

A Perl script will perform Go call graph analysis, since Go is unavailable.

The script will recursively scan .go files, parse package and import declarations, build a symbol table for internal/ symbols, resolve each call site to its target, and count distinct callers per declaration.

Import aliases, default names, and dot imports are resolved. Same-package calls stay unqualified. Cross-package calls use the import alias. Package paths are derived by joining the module prefix with the directory path relative to the repository root.

Symbols will be keyed by import path plus receiver and method name, or function name alone. Method signatures will include pointer receivers. A pre-existing catalog.json in /bench/out may provide useful analysis data.

2. **Calls vs declarations** — Stripped comments/strings, walked each function body (and nested `func` literals), and matched call syntax `name(` and `pkg.name(` only (not `func name` declarations).
3. **Import resolution** — Resolved qualified calls via `import` aliases to module paths (`github.com/usememos/memos/...`).
